transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, um, thank you for seeing me. I guess I'm here because the doctor at the general clinic got a little... well, they seemed a bit concerned about my eating habits? I'm not really sure why, honestly. I hope it's okay that I came in. 

Most days I just keep it really simple, you know? I have coffee in the morning, and then maybe just a few bites of something small between painting jobs. And then just a small dinner, especially if I'm not too busy catching up on paperwork for my college classes. That sounds pretty normal for someone with a busy schedule, right?
Do you think you are at a healthy weight?

Um, well... I guess I think I'm fine? I mean, I really don't think my weight is some kind of emergency like everyone keeps acting. It honestly feels like they're making a huge deal out of nothing. I'm just being disciplined, you know? And I'm always on my feet with painting, plus studying... it just keeps me moving. Is it so wrong to just be focused and busy? I feel like I'm doing okay, don't you think?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Um... I don't know if "afraid" is exactly the right word. I just try to be careful, I guess? 

I mean... if I eat something really heavy, like a big sandwich or pizza, I do get this... sort of panicky feeling. Just this worry that I'm going to wake up bigger, and... slower. And with my job, I have to be up and down ladders all day, moving around tight rooms and hauling equipment. If I'm heavier or sluggish, I just won't be able to move around the ladders and rooms the way I need to. 

I just want to do a good job and stay light on my feet. That makes sense, right? It's pretty normal to want to stay in shape for your work, isn't it?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't do that. I try to be really good about my portions, you know? 

Eating a huge amount of food all at once just... I think that would make me feel awful, especially if I had to get right back up on a ladder or focus on my schoolwork after. I really just prefer to stick to my normal routine and keep things very controlled. That's the right way to do it, isn't it? Just keeping everything steady and moderate?
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?

Oh, no, no. I would never do that. 

I mean, throwing up is just so... messy, and it's really bad for your teeth, isn't it? I read that somewhere. I try to take really good care of myself, so I wouldn't do something like that. If I feel like I've maybe eaten a little too much, I just make sure I'm extra active the next day at work, or I'll go for a long walk. 

That's a much healthier way to handle things, right? Just balancing it out with exercise?
Do you think your weight or body shape has any impact on your self-worth?

Um... I don't really think so? I mean, I try not to let it. 

I guess I just... I like feeling capable, you know? Like I can handle my job and my classes and just... keep everything running smoothly. If I feel good in my body, and I'm moving well at work, then I feel like I'm doing a good job. But I wouldn't say my whole self-worth is tied up in it. 

It's just about feeling healthy and productive. That's a good thing to focus on, right? Being productive?
Do you think about a specific body shape or appearance that you want to maintain through your eating habits?

Um... no, not really. I don't have like, a certain picture in my head or anything like that. 

I just... I want to look neat and put together, you know? Since I'm up and down ladders all day painting, I mostly just want to feel light and fit enough to do my job without struggling. I'm not trying to look like a magazine model or anything extreme like that. Just... appropriate and healthy. 

That's a pretty normal way to look at it, isn't it? Just wanting to stay in good shape for work?
Is there a specific weight that you try to maintain?

Um... no, not a specific number. I don't really obsess over the scale or anything like that. 

I mostly just go by how my clothes fit, you know? Like my work overalls. As long as they feel comfortable and I can move around easily on the ladders, I figure I'm doing okay. I don't think it's very healthy to get too fixated on an exact number, do you? I just try to stay in a general range that feels... right for my body and my job. 

That makes sense, doesn't it? Not worrying too much about the actual scale?
Do you think gaining a small amount of weight, like a few pounds, would be very upsetting to you?

Um... well, I wouldn't say *very* upsetting. I mean, a few pounds isn't a big deal in the grand scheme of things, right? 

But... I guess I do get a little anxious sometimes if I feel like I might be putting on weight. Like, if I eat something really heavy, you know, like pizza or a big sandwich or something, I get this... this sort of panicky feeling. Just a little one! I just start worrying that I'll wake up feeling bigger and... slower. 

And then I worry I won't be able to move around the ladders and the rooms as easily as I need to for my painting. It's just... it's really important to me to be efficient at work. That's a pretty normal thing to worry about, right? Wanting to make sure your diet doesn't interfere with your job?
Would you say that the idea of gaining weight is something that you often think about or worry about?

Um... I don't know if I'd say I *often* think about it. I try not to dwell on it too much, really. 

But... yeah, I guess it does cross my mind, especially like I was saying before... if I eat something heavy, like a big sandwich or pizza. That's when I get that little panicky feeling, you know? Just worrying that I'll wake up bigger and slower, and then I won't be able to move around the ladders and rooms the way I need to for my painting. 

But I think anyone would worry about that a little bit if it affected their work, right? It's just about being practical, don't you think?
Do you feel like your eating habits are also influenced by how you want to look in general, outside of just feeling capable and efficient for your job?

Um... no, not really. I don't think it's about looks. I mean, I try to look presentable, of course, but I'm not... I'm not trying to look like a model or anything like that. 

I just... I think it's mostly about feeling good in my own skin and being able to do what I need to do. I don't really care about being super thin just for the sake of it. That sounds kind of shallow, doesn't it? I'd rather just focus on being healthy and active. That's a better way to look at it, right?
Do you feel like your eating habits are limiting your social life or activities outside of work?

Um... no, not really limiting. I mean, I'm still doing everything I need to do. I'm still showing up for all my painting jobs, and I'm going to my classes at the college, so it's not like I'm hiding away or anything. 

I guess... well, maybe I have been skipping out on a few things lately. Like, sometimes the other painters will grab lunch together, or people from class want to meet up to study, and... I just usually say I'm busy. It's just... it feels a little easier right now to just keep my routine tight, you know? 

It's not that I don't want to see them. It's just... sometimes people can be kind of nosy about what you're eating or not eating, and I'd just rather avoid the comments. It's just easier to focus on my work and my classes that way. That makes sense, right? It's pretty normal to just want to stick to your own schedule sometimes?
Do you feel like your eating habits are affecting your relationships with friends or family?

Um... no, I wouldn't say they're affecting my relationships. I mean, my family and I are still close, and I still talk to my friends. 

I guess... well, my mom has made a few comments lately, just asking if I'm eating enough because she thinks I look a little tired. But moms always worry about that kind of stuff, right? It's just her being a mom. And sometimes my friends will ask why I'm not eating when we do end up hanging out, but I usually just tell them I already ate or that I'm not feeling well. 

I don't think it's causing any real problems, though. I'm still there for them when they need me, and we still have good conversations. It's just a minor thing, you know? I'm sure it's nothing to be concerned about, right?
Are there any activities you enjoy doing in your free time that you've stopped doing or are doing less often because of your eating habits?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I've stopped doing anything I enjoy. I mean, I still love painting, obviously, and I still like to read and go for walks when I have the time. 

I guess... I haven't been going to the community center for the pottery classes I used to take on weekends. But that's mostly just because I've been so busy with work and my regular classes, you know? It's not really about my eating habits or anything like that. I just... I need to make sure I have enough energy for the things that really matter, like my job and school. 

It's pretty normal to let a hobby slide when you have a lot on your plate, right? I'm sure I'll get back into it eventually when things slow down a bit. That's a reasonable way to handle a busy schedule, isn't it?
Do you ever feel like you can't stop eating once you start?

Um... no, definitely not. I don't really have that problem at all. 

Actually, it's... it's kind of the opposite for me. I feel like I have a really good handle on what I'm eating. I'm very careful about my portions and making sure I don't overdo it. I like to feel in control of things, you know? It just makes me feel a bit more grounded when everything else is so busy.

I don't ever really get that feeling where I just lose control and can't stop. I'm pretty disciplined about it. That's a good thing, right? Being mindful and having self-control with food... that's what we're supposed to do to stay healthy, isn't it?
Do you feel like your eating habits are causing you a lot of stress or anxiety?

Um... no, I wouldn't say they cause me stress. Honestly, it's... it's kind of the opposite? Knowing exactly what I'm going to eat and keeping it all, you know, structured... it actually helps me feel less anxious. 

My job can be pretty demanding—painting and hanging wallpaper all day, trying to keep clients happy and meet deadlines—so having my food perfectly planned out just gives me one less thing to worry about. It keeps me grounded when the rest of my day is chaotic. 

I mean, being organized like that is a good thing, don't you think? A lot of people are strict with their routines to avoid stress, right? I'm just trying to manage everything the best I can so I don't get overwhelmed. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you think you would be very upset if you gained a significant amount of weight?

Um... I mean, I think anyone would be a little upset, right? It's just... I have a really physical job. 

If I were to gain a lot of weight, it would just make things so much harder for me. Like, if I even just eat something heavy, you know, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this... this panicky feeling. I just worry that I'll wake up feeling bigger and slower, and then I won't be able to move around the ladders and rooms the way I need to for work. 

I have to be light on my feet to do my job well. So, worrying about gaining weight... it's really just about wanting to be good at what I do and stay capable. That's a normal thing to worry about when your job is so physical, isn't it? I just want to make sure I can keep working hard.
Do you think you would feel less anxious about your eating if you weren't worried about how it might affect your weight or body shape?

Um... I suppose maybe I would? I mean, like I was saying just a minute ago... if I didn't get that awful panicky feeling after eating something heavy, worrying that I'll wake up bigger and not be able to move around my ladders properly... then yeah, I probably wouldn't stress about my meals as much. 

If I didn't have to worry about staying light and fast for my painting jobs, I guess eating wouldn't feel quite so... loaded. But I really just see it as being responsible, you know? It's not so much about vanity, it's just wanting to be capable and do a good job for my clients. Wanting to stay in the right shape for a physical job is pretty normal, right? I'm just trying to be a good worker... I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like your eating habits are significantly impacting your overall quality of life?

Um... impacting my quality of life? I wouldn't say significantly, no. I mean, I'm still getting everything I need to get done. 

I'm still showing up for all my painting jobs, and I'm taking a couple of college classes right now too, and I haven't missed any of those. So I'm still completely responsible. I guess... well, I have sort of started avoiding, like, lunches with the other contractors on site, or those study meetups people do after class. 

But it's really just because it feels easier? It's just simpler to keep my routine tight and... and not have people commenting on what I'm doing or what I brought for lunch. It just avoids any awkwardness, you know? 

I think it's pretty normal to just want to eat in peace and stay focused on your work or school, don't you? It doesn't really affect my life in a bad way, as long as I'm still doing a good job and getting good grades... right?
Are there any activities or social events that you avoid because you're worried about gaining weight?

Um... well, like I mentioned just a moment ago, I guess I have been avoiding some things... like when the other contractors go out for lunch, or when people from my classes want to get together to study. 

It's not exactly that I'm terrified of gaining weight right in that moment, it's just... it's just easier to stick to my own routine, you know? If I go out, I have to worry about what kind of food is going to be there, and if it's something heavy that's going to make me feel slow and ruin my work day. And then people always want to talk about what you're eating, or why you aren't eating what they're eating, and it just gets so awkward. 

So, I do avoid those things, but I'm still showing up for all my jobs and my classes. I'm still doing what I'm supposed to do. It's just better for me to eat alone so I don't have to deal with the comments and I can just stay focused. That's a pretty reasonable way to handle it, don't you think? I'm just trying to avoid unnecessary stress so I can keep being a good worker and student.
